transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Srinivasan (Redwood SE), Malik Torres (Redwood PM), Markus Vale (Havenly CISO), Sara Kim (Havenly SecEng), Liam O'Neill (Head of IT), Dana Ruiz (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick posture review for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 artifacts, trust center access, controls mapping, KMS/encryption, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, and data residency questions. Action items captured and follow-up technical deep-dive requested.

Topics:
- Report access (SOC 2 Type II, ISO certificates)
- Controls mapping (customer controls -> Redwood controls)
- Trust center access and pen test reports
- SSO/SAML and RBAC model
- Encryption at rest / in transit, KMS integration
- Data residency and private deployment options

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, and—uh—quick intro?
[00:08] Markus (Havenly - CISO): yeah Markus here, thanks. We wanted to run through your SOC2/ISO posture, see what we can see for our compliance team, especially around KMS and audit logs.
[00:17] Jordan: perfect, Priya will lead the technical bits, i'll handle logistics and next steps.
[00:21] Priya (Redwood SE): hi all, thanks. quick note: transcription may mangle some acronyms, sorry in advance if you see Sam-el or SBAC spelled weirdly in notes.
[00:30] Sara (Havenly): ha yeah we get that from other tools too. ok let's jump in. first question: do you provide full SOC 2 Type II report access or just a summary?
[00:40] Jordan: we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and our ISO 27001 cert, we host artifacts in our trust center. i'll share the secure link after this call — short link is https://redwood.com/trust but we'll send an enterprise access link.
[00:53] Liam (Havenly): when you say redacted, do you remove vendor details and customer identifiers? our procurement needs at least control narratives and the test-of-controls results.
[01:05] Jordan: yes, the redaction removes other customer PII and vendor-specific attachments; control narratives and test-of-controls summaries are included. if you need field-level logs or raw evidence we can arrange an NDA and limited-access share.
[01:20] Markus: what about the controls mapping? we maintain a mapping to our internal control IDs and we need to see how Redwood's controls map to ISO 27001 and SOC criteria.
[01:30] Priya: we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet — it's usually a CSV that maps Redwood control IDs to SOC Trust Service Criteria and ISO 27001 Annex A controls. i'll attach that and highlight the ones most relevant to data residency, encryption, and access control.
[01:44] Markus: ok great. do you have a short example?
[01:47] Priya: yes, e.g., we map our 'Identity and Access Management' control to SOC CC6 and ISO A.9 – you'll see the narrative and sample evidence links. note: sometimes our tool spits 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' in transcripts — but the actual docs are clean.
[02:05] Sara: ha, noted. next: SSO/SAML support — we use Okta. we want SCIM provisioning, SAML2 SSO, and fine-grained RBAC. what does Redwood support?
[02:16] Priya: Okta SAML SSO is supported out of the box, SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync, and we have role-based access controls in the Console. roles can be mapped to groups from IdP. for dedicated/private deployments we can integrate with customer LDAP/AD as well.
[02:34] Liam: does it support attribute-based access or just group->role mapping?
[02:39] Priya: currently group-to-role is primary; we can support additional claim-based rules as a configuration for enterprise customers — it's a config in the control plane. i'll capture the exact attribute mappings in the follow-up doc.
[02:50] Markus: audit logs — how granular are they? we need admin changes, API calls, model inference request metadata (not the actual prompt content), and retention policies.
[03:01] Malik (Redwood PM): our audit logs include admin actions (create/delete/service-config), API request metadata (timestamp, model id, token usage, route), and console UI actions. we do not include full customer prompt content in logs by default; that is protected. retention can be configured per plan and for Private deployments you can export to your SIEM.
[03:21] Sara: can we ship logs to our Splunk instance or to a cloud storage bucket?
[03:26] Malik: yes — we support log forwarding to syslog/HTTPS endpoints, Cloud Storage (GCS/AWS S3) with encryption, or direct SIEM integration for enterprise. for hosted customers we offer a managed retention policy.
[03:38] Dana (Procurement): on encryption — do you use KMS? how do you manage keys for hosted vs private?
[03:44] Priya: good question. hosted: we manage keys using a cloud KMS (customer data encrypted by Redwood-managed keys). for enterprise we offer customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault integrations; for private or on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs. keys can be rotated on a schedule or on demand.
[04:02] Markus: is there a Bring-Your-Own-Key option where we control the key lifecycle?
[04:07] Priya: yes, BYOK via KMS, you control rotation and access policies; Redwood requests the minimal permissions needed to use the key for encrypt/decrypt; we also support envelope encryption if you require HSM-backed key wrapping.
[04:18] Jordan: i'll include the KMS integration guide and a short diagram in the follow-up.
[04:23] [pause — ~1 minute of side channel audio, transcription a bit messy]
[05:30] Sara: data residency — we have EU patients and PHI, we need data at rest to be in EU, and controls to prevent cross-region replication. how do Redwood regions work?
[05:43] Priya: Redwood has region pins for model hosting and data plane. Hosted customers can choose a region for processing; Dedicated or Private deployments provide full regional isolation. for EU residency we put inference and storage in EU cloud regions and disable cross-region backups unless explicitly requested.
[06:01] Liam: is metadata (like logs or usage metrics) ever stored in US for analytics?
[06:06] Malik: by default usage analytics may be aggregated in a central telemetry store; for enterprise customers we offer an option to restrict telemetry to the selected region or to export telemetry to your own storage to satisfy residency constraints.
[06:20] Markus: one of our requirements is documented evidence for change management and vulnerability scanning — weekly or monthly scans and patch windows. do you publish pen test reports or scan cadence?
[06:33] Priya: we publish summaries of pen test results in the trust center and can share redacted pen test reports under NDA. we run vulnerability scanning on code and infra regularly; critical findings have a documented SLA for remediation, and the SOC 2 report includes attestations about vulnerability management.
[06:50] Sara: do you do third-party code dependencies scanning for supply-chain risk?
[06:54] Malik: yes, we run SCA (software composition analysis) and track dependencies. we can share our SBOM summary and the policy for dependency updates.
[07:05] Markus: for ISO 27001 specifically, do you have Annex A mapping and an ISMS scope document?
[07:12] Priya: yes, ISO cert plus scope doc and Annex A mapping are in the trust center; i'll include the scope (it's infra + control plane + hosted inference, not customer's private VPC unless under a Private deployment).
[07:26] Liam: audit frequency — when was last ISO surveillance and is the cert current?
[07:31] Jordan: our ISO surveillance was in June 2026 and the cert is current through 2027 — full details in the cert we will share.
[07:40] Sara: incident response playbooks and breach notification timelines?
[07:43] Malik: we maintain an IR runbook; standard SLA is 72 hours for notification to customers for confirmed incidents, 24 hours for customer-impacting incidents. we also publish SOC incident metrics in the trust portal.
[07:59] Markus: do you have a dedicated security contact or a vCISO for enterprise customers?
[08:03] Jordan: we assign a security liaison and the SE/PM are available for technical review. for enterprise we can set up a named security contact and escalation path.
[08:12] Dana: procurement question — are there any carve-outs or liabilities around data processed in model outputs? we need to list in contract.
[08:21] Jordan: yes, we normally have data processing and liability clauses; procurement will review after we share security artifacts. i'll loop legal after we share the reports.
[08:29] Sara: one more technical: can we run model evaluation locally or run a canary on our Dedicated capacity for a subset of traffic? we need to test privacy-sensitive prompts.
[08:40] Priya: Dedicated supports traffic pinning and canary rules; you can route a percentage to a dedicated pool or to a private deployment. we also support on-prem package for fully air-gapped evaluation.
[08:53] Liam: latency and telemetry during canary — will you expose per-request metadata?
[08:58] Malik: yes per-request metrics (latency, token counts) are available; payloads are not exported by default, but you can enable detailed tracing under an agreement.
[09:10] [brief cross talk about support SLA tiers and pricing — lines omitted]
[12:05] Jordan: sounds like the immediate asks are: 1) share SOC2/ISO artifacts, 2) controls mapping CSV, 3) KMS integration guide, 4) trust center link and pen test redacted report under NDA. we'll capture action items.
[12:20] Markus: yes and our security team will want a technical deep-dive the following week.
[12:24] Priya: happy to schedule a 60-minute technical session with your sec engs — we can do hands-on config and SCIM/SAML mapping.
[12:30] Sara: good. also please note we may want a written assurance about not storing prompts in logs and exact retention windows.
[12:39] Priya: we'll include the retention matrix in the follow-up and the export options to your SIEM.
[12:44] Markus: any known gaps or exceptions we should be aware of for SOC 2?
[12:49] Jordan: we track exceptions in the SOC report; the summary will flag any scope exclusions or compensating controls. we'll call them out when we send over the report.
[12:59] Dana: timeline wise procurement wants everything by the end of next week so legal can review — is that reasonable?
[13:06] Jordan: yes, we'll aim to have the core artifacts in the next 48-72 hours.
[13:12] Priya: I'll send controls mapping and a draft of the SCIM attribute mapping by Friday.
[13:18] Markus: great. one last thing — do you support customer-managed logging endpoints with encryption in transit and at rest? we want TLS + S3 SSE-KMS.
[13:28] Malik: yes, logs to S3 with SSE-KMS is supported; we'll document the exact params.
[13:33] Jordan: ok let's run through quick recap and owners.
[13:36] [RECAP]
[13:37] Jordan: Jordan to send SOC2 Type II and ISO cert (redacted) — due 2026-11-06.
[13:42] Priya: Priya to send controls mapping CSV, KMS integration guide, and SCIM attribute mapping — due 2026-11-07.
[13:49] Markus: Havenly to give list of compliance must-haves and any contractual clauses — due 2026-11-10.
[13:56] Dana: procurement to confirm NDA and timeline — due 2026-11-08.
[14:02] Jordan: schedule follow-up technical deep-dive week of 2026-11-09 — Jordan to propose times.
[14:09] Sara: thanks everyone; appreciate the thoroughness.
[14:12] Jordan: thanks folks, we'll follow up in Slack/email. bye.

End of transcript.
